نَاشِزٌ Rising; or rising from its place; high, or elevated; protuberant, or prominent; protruding. (K, * TA.) You say, قَلْبٌ نَاشِزٌ A heart rising from its place by reason of fright. (K, TA.) And تَلٌّ نَاشِزٌ A high, or an elevated, mound, or hill: pl. [reg. of نَاشِزَةٌ and irreg. of نَاشِزٌ] نَوَاشِزُ. (TA.) And رَكَبٌ نَاشِزٌ A protuberant, high, pubes, or mons Veneris. (TA.) And لَحْمَةٌ نَاشِزَةٌ A piece of flesh elevated, or protuberant, upon the body. (TA.) And عِرْقٌ نَاشِزٌ A vein constantly swollen and pulsating (A, K *) in consequence of disease (K, TA) or from some other cause. (TA.) And رَجُلٌ نَاشِزُ الجَبْهَةِ A man having a high, or prominent, forehead. (TA.) And إِمْرَأَةٌ نَاشِزَةُ القُصَيْرَى A woman large in the sides, having the قصيرى [or lowest of the ribs] with the flesh upon it, prominent. (IAar, TA.) ＝
-A2- Also, (A, TA,) or نَاشِزَةٌ, (Mgh,) [but the former is the more common,] (tropical:) A woman disobedient to her husband, (Mgh, TA,) and exalting herself against him, (TA,) and hating him, (Mgh, TA,) and deserting him. (TA.) See 1. [The former epithet is also applied in like manner to a husband.]
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
